title: Orchestrate control-plane canary upgrades using Terraform modules and automated health gating
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: Private (VPC) deployments currently require manual control-plane upgrades: operators update a Terraform variable, run apply, and then monitor until all nodes report the new version. This is error-prone at scale (per-customer private stacks) and provides no structured canary gating or automated rollback.

Objective: Implement an automated, Terraform-driven canary upgrade process for the control plane that: (1) encodes control-plane versioning into IaC modules, (2) creates a dedicated canary subset for early verification, (3) wires health checks and SLAs into promotion/rollback automation, and (4) integrates with our CI/CD (GitHub Actions) and Console dashboards so operators get visibility and manual override.

High-level approach and design decisions: 
- Versioning: adopt strict control-plane semantic versioning (major.minor.patch) and require every upgrade to be initiated by bumping modules/control_plane variable control_plane_version (e.g., 1.18.2 -> 1.19.0). The module will write the active version to a SSM Parameter (per-customer) and tag compute resources for inventory.
- Canary topology: extend the control_plane Terraform module to create a small canary ASG/instance-pool (default 1-2 nodes) that can be launched with the new version in parallel to the stable pool. Traffic shaping to canary will be handled via the private router: we introduce a per-stack target group with weighted routing or, where not possible, route a percentage of health-check/heartbeat probes plus a small fraction of real traffic through a side proxy in the customer VPC.
- Promotion strategy: automated progressive rollouts: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% by default, with configurable steps. Each step is gated by health signals and quality checks for a configurable observation window.
- Health signals: rely on three classes of checks: 1) infra health (/healthz readiness, restarted pods count), 2) performance metrics (p50/p95 inference latency, request success rate), and 3) functional correctness (a small set of replayed prompts / evals executed by the upgrade harness). The Terraform module will create CloudWatch (or equivalent) metric filters and alarms for each stack that are used by the promotion engine.
- Promotion engine: a lightweight workflow implemented as a GitHub Actions workflow + AWS Step Function OR internal runbook lambda (prototype as GH Actions). The engine runs after terraform apply for canary, evaluates metrics via CloudWatch and the eval harness (calls Console eval API), and decides to proceed, pause for manual approval, or rollback.
- Rollback policy: automated rollback if any step exceeds thresholds for more than the observation window, or if eval harness indicates quality regression. Rollback is implemented by Terraform: revert control_plane_version variable and reapply to return fleet to previous known-good configuration.
- State and safety: use remote state (S3 with DynamoDB locking). All cross-stack changes are applied with plan + apply and require non-empty apply approvals for promotion to >20% by default.

Terraform module changes (implementation notes):
- modules/control_plane: add variables: control_plane_version (string), canary_enabled (bool), canary_instance_count (int), canary_traffic_weight (float list for steps), observation_windows (list), eval_job_name (string).
- modules/control_plane/resources: create resources for canary ASG / instance-pool named "canary"; create or extend target group(s) / routing rules to support weighted traffic; add IAM role for the promotion engine to query metrics and trigger eval runs.
- outputs: control_plane_active_version (string), canary_endpoint (string), canary_instance_ids (list). Because our JSON schema cannot nest, the module will expose these via SSM and tags in addition to outputs.
- remote state: ensure each private stack has namespaced state file and locking to prevent concurrent upgrades.

Canary gating criteria (defaults):
- Infra: healthz success rate >= 99.5% for observation window (10m per step). No more than 1 restart per instance in window.
- Performance: p95 latency not increase by >50ms from baseline and p50 not increase by >20ms.
- Errors: 5xx error rate < 0.1% delta vs baseline.
- Eval quality: automated eval suite must show no regression above a 1% tolerance for configured key prompts (configurable per-customer).

Automation flow (ops-friendly):
1) Engineer/SE updates modules/control_plane variable control_plane_version in repo and opens PR.
2) CI runs plan; Terraform plan creates a canary ASG and marks canary resources in plan output.
3) On merge, GitHub Actions applies canary-only change (modules create canary resources and new version tags).
4) Promotion engine polls metrics for step window. If all gates pass, engine updates Terraform variable canary_traffic_weight to move to next step and triggers terraform apply (or issues API call to ALB to shift weights). Steps repeat until 100% or a pause/rollback occurs.
5) For multi-tenant private instances we keep canaries per-customer. For customers who want no canary we provide a flag to do rolling in-place via instance draining.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for Terraform module via Terratest, including canary ASG creation, tagging, and output invariants.
- Integration test: create a dedicated QA private stack, run scheduled upgrade with synthetic traffic that verifies health checks and eval harness integration.
- Chaos test: introduce CPU latency on canary nodes and assert that automation detects degradation and rolls back.
- Dry-run in staging with feature flag: disable actual traffic shift but validate resource creation and alarm triggers.

CI/CD and operational controls: 
- GitHub Actions workflow: upgrade-canary.yml that performs: plan, apply (canary only), wait/gate loop, promote steps via PR with "promote" label for manual override.
- Approval policy: promotion beyond 20% requires at least one approver from Platform. Option to set stricter policies per-customer via stack variables.
- Console: add "control plane version" card and history to Console inventory to show which stacks are on which versions and canary status. Hook in audit log when promotions happen.

Monitoring and runbooks:
- Dashboards: add stacked timeline showing versions vs request latency and error spikes per stack.
- Alarms: CloudWatch alarms created by module include SNS topic subscription to oncall.
- Runbook: document steps to force rollback, emergency abort (terminate canary ASG and revert variable), and how to reconcile state if apply fails mid-promotion. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Control+Plane+Upgrade+Playbook (WIP).

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Weighted routing support varies across customer networking topologies; some customers will require a proxy-based traffic-shift rather than ALB weights. We need a pluggable adapter in modules.
- Full blue/green vs incremental canary: blue/green is faster for rollback but costlier (double capacity). We default to canary but expose blue/green flag per-stack.
- Eval harness cost: calling functional evals on every step may increase cost for large fleets. Consider sampling or a small representative prompt set per-customer.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Terraform module change merged and tested with Terratest.
- A staging private stack successfully completes a canary upgrade from 1.18.2 -> 1.19.0 using the automated promotion engine without manual intervention.
- Promotion engine correctly halts and rolls back when synthetic faults are introduced.
- Console shows per-stack version and canary status; audit events for promotions are recorded.

Links and artifacts: 
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canary+Upgrades+RFC (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3291 (prototype terraform module + GH Actions)
- Eval harness job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/actions/runs/87234
- Staging dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade-flow/staging-control-plane-upgrades
